title: Low-distortion cardinal versus ordinal mechanisms
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Historical question, answered affirmatively in the cited 2018 paper: can truthful cardinal voting mechanisms have distortion O(√(m log m)) while exhibiting behavior unavailable to truthful ordinal mechanisms? More precisely, there is a family of mechanisms μₙ,ₘ for all n≥1 voters and m≥3 alternatives, with a universal distortion bound C√(m log m), truthful in expectation, whose component for n=1 and m=3 violates both non-perversity and localization as defined below. These are the source’s concrete meanings of the extracted phrase “very different”. This is already a result of the source, not its neighboring open question about the optimal distortion.
context:
The saved sentence occurs immediately after a separate open distortion-gap question. Its next sentences announce the randomized hyperspherical mechanism and its affirmative answer to the structural comparison. Section 3.2 proves the welfare bound in Theorem 15 and exhibits failures of non-perversity and localization.

Cardinal reporting permits numerical utilities, but truthfulness still restricts which welfare guarantees a mechanism can achieve. The source proves a general Ω(√m) distortion lower bound and gives the O(√(m log m)) construction. Its structural result shows that this upper-bound scale does not force the two ordinal properties.

The source uses strict, nonnegative, unit-sum utility vectors and dominant-strategy truthfulness in expectation. Unit-range utilities, approximate truthfulness and equilibrium welfare for manipulable mechanisms are different models, also discussed in the article.

references.title: On the Welfare of Cardinal Voting Mechanisms
references.locator: Unresolved-question passage on page 4; PDF page 4

definitions: Let A={1,…,m} and let Uₘ consist of vectors u∈[0,1]ᵐ with ∑ₐu(a)=1 and pairwise distinct coordinates. Reports and true utilities both range over Uₘ. A cardinal mechanism μ:Uₘⁿ→Δ(A) selects one alternative with its specified probabilities; there are no payments. Write μ(u)(a) for the probability of a. Truthfulness in expectation means that for every profile u, voter i and alternative report v∈Uₘ, ∑ₐuᵢ(a)μ(u)(a)≥∑ₐuᵢ(a)μ(u₋ᵢ,v)(a). Thus truth telling is a dominant strategy regardless of other reports. Social welfare is SWᵤ(a)=∑ᵢuᵢ(a). Distortion is the supremum over all u∈Uₘⁿ of maxₐSWᵤ(a)/∑ₐμ(u)(a)SWᵤ(a), with a zero denominator giving +∞. The constant C is independent of n,m and utilities; log may be taken as the natural logarithm. An ordinal mechanism depends only on the strict ranking induced by each utility vector. The source extends non-perversity to cardinal mechanisms by requiring that changing one report v to v′, with v′(a)>v(a) and the relative order of all alternatives other than a unchanged, never decreases the probability of a. Localization requires that whenever the same set B is the top k alternatives in v and v′ and ∑ₐ∈Bv(a)=∑ₐ∈Bv′(a), changing that one report preserves the total probability assigned to B. Both requirements quantify over all other voters’ fixed reports. A violation is a pair of legal reports and fixed other reports failing the corresponding inequality or equality. No running-time or finite-precision input condition is imposed by this structural existence question.
answer_criterion: The affirmative result consists of a mechanism family with the uniform distortion bound and exact incentive guarantee, together with violations of both specified properties in its three-alternative, one-voter component. The cited Section 3.2 supplies this result. Improving the general optimal-distortion bounds is a separate question and is not needed to answer this historical card.
